title: An example reveals an answer’s limits

captions.physics: Testing a thought through a trial
captions.energy: Releasing an explanation that is exhausted
captions.emotions: Feeling a familiar picture break apart

meaning: A practical example can help you end an outdated explanation even when discovering its limits feels emotionally unsettling.
text: A thought may look dependable until you try giving it a form. The Empress in the physical position of Ajna suggests making an example and seeing the result for yourselves. Death in energy supports willingness to end an explanation that no longer fits the task and move towards fresh understanding. The Tower in emotions describes the abrupt feeling of a familiar picture losing its foundation. Absorbing the discovery may be difficult even while reconsideration can release the question from an answer that has run its course.

Imagine preparing a short presentation of a shared idea. A trial slide containing the main points reveals that the promised result belongs to a different task altogether. **A visible example lets an explanation end when it no longer holds.** At first, the collected phrases and attractive sequence feel difficult to lose. Yet you can now understand why the account was hard to finish. You can seek an accurate description of your actual intention while preserving useful observations and acknowledging that the account’s original centre has changed. The surprise acquires a specific subject.

The difficulty is moving from intense disappointment to a conclusion that the idea itself has no value. Ending an inaccurate version then reaches beyond what the example revealed. Willingness to release an exhausted account remains useful when you distinguish the explanation from its subject. Reconsideration can be substantial while leaving a living intention room to find another form and more accurate words.
